explanations: The defect is `return ENOENT;` in courier_pick. The whole module reports errors as negative errno values (-ENOENT, -EINVAL, -ENOMEM), and dispatch_batch tells them apart with `idx == -ENOENT` and `idx < 0`. A positive ENOENT (2) when the courier list is empty is indistinguishable from the valid index 2, so dispatch_batch increments `couriers[2].load` and reads `couriers[2].id`, which is out of bounds when there are no couriers. The result is memory corruption or a crash instead of every order being left unassigned. The fix is `return -ENOENT;`.

All orders are validated in a first loop, before the result array is allocated and before any load is incremented, so the whole batch is rejected with nothing mutated. *out is set to NULL at the top and only assigned on success, so the caller has nothing to free. The other choices describe a design that validates and assigns in one pass, which this code does not do.

courier_pick returns -ENOENT when every courier is full; dispatch_batch treats that as 'skip this order' and continues, so the batch succeeds with 0 assignments. In run_dispatch_cycle rc is 0, so the unassigned message is printed with 5 of 5, the `rc > 0` guard skips publishing, and free(assignments) runs on the way out. Running out of capacity is not an error condition, nothing is published with empty entries, and the code never waits.

In the failure branch the code frees `assignments` and returns prc, so there is no leak and the caller sees the negative errno. Nothing in this code decrements courier->load, so those increments from dispatch_batch persist even though the assignments were not published. The function does not return rc in that branch, so the caller does not see success.
